alt_texts: Core 60, number 1 of 60: Animals in the news, asked 25 times in UPSC Prelims. Bar chart of questions per year from 2016 to 2026. Aarav asks if he should memorise every animal in the news; Priya says most questions ask how and where they live.
The pattern: the news picks the animal, UPSC tests how it lives. Of 25 questions, 11 ask how it lives and behaves, 8 where it lives, 3 what it is, 3 other. Three of the 25 are about plants.

UPSC's traps: 'only' is easy to break, since one-horned rhinos also live in Nepal and only the Asiatic lion is India-only. 'Some' is easy to satisfy. Names mislead: the froghopper is an insect and the Golden Mahseer a fish.

The latest three PYQs: 2026 Q27 on Amur falcons at Doyang, answer a, local conservation works (provisional key). 2025 Q37 on the Gooty tarantula, answer d. 2024 Q29 on toxic species in butterflies, fish and frogs, answer c, all three.

Read this first: NCERT Class 12 Biology chapters 11 and 13, and NCERT Class 10 Geography chapter 2. Skip species lists without habitats. All 25 questions explained free at minimalistias.com/upsc-syllabus/prelims.
